  "text": "The first photograph arrived on Monday. It showed me asleep in bed.

I live alone, so I called the police.

They checked the locks, searched the apartment, and suggested I change my passwords. One officer asked whether an ex still had a key.

On Tuesday, another photograph arrived.

Same bed. Same angle. This time my eyes were open.

I hadn't woken during the night.

I bought a camera and aimed it at the bedroom door. In the morning, its memory card contained eight hours of uninterrupted footage: closed door, empty hallway, nothing moving.

The third photograph showed me sitting upright, looking directly at whoever held the camera.

There was writing on the back.

YOU'RE GETTING BETTER AT IT.

I stayed at my brother's house that night. He let me sleep on the sofa and promised to stay awake.

At three, he shook me violently.

“You were standing over me,” he said.

I'd been dreaming about stairs.

We checked his doorbell camera. At 2:41, I had walked outside barefoot and faced the lens for eleven minutes.

Then I smiled and held up a photograph.

We paused the recording.

It showed my brother asleep on the sofa. I was standing over him, one hand extended toward his face.

He asked me to leave before morning.

Yesterday, an envelope arrived with no photograph inside. Just a note.

TONIGHT YOU CAN HOLD THE CAMERA.

I burned it in the kitchen sink and sat awake until dawn.

This morning there was ash on my pillow.

My brother hasn't answered his phone, and I found his spare key in my mouth."
}
